statement:
The function $f$ satisfies $0\le f(t)\le K$ when $0\le t\le x$. Explain by means of a sketch, or otherwise, why
$$0\le\int_0^x f(t)\,dt\le Kx.$$

By considering $\displaystyle\int_0^1\frac{t}{n(n-t)}\,dt$, or otherwise, show that, if $n>1$,
$$0\le\ln\left(\frac{n}{n-1}\right)-\frac1n\le\frac1{n-1}-\frac1n,$$
and deduce that
$$0\le\ln N-\sum_{n=2}^N\frac1n\le1.$$

Deduce that as $N\to\infty$,
$$\sum_{n=1}^N\frac1n\to\infty.$$

Noting that $2^{10}=1024$, show also that if $N<10^{30}$ then
$$\sum_{n=1}^N\frac1n<101.$$
solution:
**First bound.** Since $0\le f(t)\le K$ on $[0,x]$, the integral (an area) lies between $0$ and the area $Kx$ of the rectangle of height $K$ and width $x$.

**Comparing $\ln(n/(n-1))$ and $1/n$.** We compute
$$\int_0^1\frac{t}{n(n-t)}\,dt=\int_0^1\left(\frac1{n-t}-\frac1n\right)dt=\left[-\ln(n-t)-\frac tn\right]_0^1=\ln\frac{n}{n-1}-\frac1n.$$

Since the integrand is non-negative, this is $\ge0$. For the upper bound, on $[0,1]$ we have $\dfrac{t}{n-t}\le\dfrac{1}{n-1}$ (as $t\le1$ and $n-t\ge n-1$), so
$$\int_0^1\frac{t}{n(n-t)}\,dt\le\int_0^1\frac{1}{n(n-1)}\,dt=\frac{1}{n(n-1)}=\frac1{n-1}-\frac1n.$$

Thus $0\le\ln\frac{n}{n-1}-\frac1n\le\frac1{n-1}-\frac1n$.

**Summing.** Sum over $n=2,\dots,N$. The middle term telescopes ($\sum\ln\frac{n}{n-1}=\ln N$), giving
$$0\le\ln N-\sum_{n=2}^N\frac1n\le\sum_{n=2}^N\left(\frac1{n-1}-\frac1n\right)=1-\frac1N\le1.$$

**Divergence.** Since $\ln N-\sum_{n=2}^N\frac1n\le1$, we have $\sum_{n=2}^N\frac1n\ge\ln N-1\to\infty$ as $N\to\infty$. Hence $\sum_{n=1}^N\frac1n\to\infty$.

**The $10^{30}$ bound.** From $0\le\ln N-\sum_{n=2}^N\frac1n$, we get $\sum_{n=1}^N\frac1n\le1+\ln N$. If $N<10^{30}$, then $\ln N<30\ln10<30\ln1024^{\cdots}$. More simply, $\ln10<\ln1024=10\ln2$, and since $\ln2<1$ we have $\ln10<10\cdot\tfrac{69}{100}$-style bounds; concretely $30\ln10<100$, so
$$\sum_{n=1}^N\frac1n\le1+\ln N<1+30\ln10<101.$$

(Using $\ln10\approx2.303<\tfrac{10}{3}$, we get $30\ln10<100$, so $1+30\ln10<101$.)
